sentences.text: Revenue went from essentially nil in FY2021 to $5,387 million in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F3][F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue rose 2914.5% to $1,658 million as deliveries began [F4][D83][P67].
Growth then decelerated sharply, to 167.4% in FY2023, 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025 [D135][D187][D239].
The loss narrowed every year after FY2022, with operating income improving 16.3% in FY2023, 18.3% in FY2024 and 23.5% in FY2025 [D136][D188][D240].
In FY2025 Software and Services revenue grew 221.7% to $1,557 million, contributing 21.6pp of the 8.4% total growth [S26][D322][D323][D239].
That increase came primarily from vehicle electrical architecture and software development services, remarketing sales and repair and maintenance [P18].
New electric vehicle revenue fell 12.5% and subtracted 10.5pp, while Volkswagen Group revenue of $836 million added 15.4pp [D287][D288][S5][D281].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% on 9,332 fewer deliveries, due in part to the expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 [D315][P22].
Operating costs grew 1.5pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 6.9%, and incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D266][D258][D265].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7% in FY2025, above the -45.8% window median and the -845.5% window low [F19][D332][D330].
Operating margin of -66.5% is the window high but still far below the -1.6% autos peer median [F31][D325][D344].
The 26.8pp operating-margin gain in FY2025 came almost entirely from cost of revenue, helped by fewer vehicles produced and lower raw material and conversion costs [D267][P21].
In FY2025 net margin of -67.7% sat 1.1pp below the -66.5% operating margin, with other expense of $54 million partly from a $186 million litigation settlement [F43][F31][D359][X84][P10].
Operating cash flow of -$779 million was far short of the -$3,646 million net loss, and free cash flow was -$2,489 million, a -46.2% margin [F64][F38][F78][D226].
The improvement in operating cash use was primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1,710 million, 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A, on Normal Factory capacity expansion [D246][F71][D225][D228][P3].
Stock-based compensation of $741 million was 13.8% of revenue and 20.7% of the operating loss [X56][D223][D237].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million in FY2025 from $3,259 million, as cash and investments dropped 21.0% to $6,082 million against $4,440 million of debt [D231][D179][D261][D229][D230].
The current ratio fell to 2.33x, the window low, from a 4.94x window median [F129][D339][D341].
Financing inflow of $886 million included $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group on the Financial Milestone [F92][P2].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% to 1,186 million, so EPS improved 34.5% while net loss fell 23.2% [D260][X91][D242][D241].
Net losses ran seven consecutive years, from -$426 million in FY2019 to -$3,646 million in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
The loss is narrowing but the accumulated deficit of $27.0 billion shows how much capital the model has consumed [P5].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223][D31].
That dilution is a recurring cost of retaining staff rather than a one-off.
Cash and investments cover 2.4 years of the latest burn [R3][D236].
With capex rising and the R2 launch ahead, the runway is the constraint that matters most [P31].
Whether gross margin holds above the FY2025 2.7% level in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the cost trend [F19].
Whether operating cash flow use narrows below the FY2025 -$779 million in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the burn trend [F64].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the FY2025 30.5% level in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the liquidity cushion [D232].
